issues.detail: The Greek 'φλυαρων ημας' (speaking/babbling to us) is translated as 'nói xấu chúng tôi' (speaking ill of us/slandering us). The Greek implies the act of speaking/babbling, not necessarily the specific content of slandering.

The Greek 'ουτε αυτος επιδεχεται' (nor does he receive) is rendered as 'người ấy cũng không tiếp nhận', but the 'neither/nor' structure of 'ουτε... και' is slightly flattened. More importantly, the Vietnamese 'ngăn cấm những người muốn tiếp nhận' translates 'τους βουλομενους κωλυει' (hinders those who want [to come]), missing the implicit object of 'wanting to join/come' which is implied by the context of 'receiving'.
